newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner oil group awaits deals - report.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner oil group awaits deals - report.

text.p: The oil and gas division of Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner ASA has been shortlisted for projects worth 30 billion crowns, according to a report by an Oslo-based brokerage house.
All of the contracts are due to be awarded within the next six months, the report said.
"It's roughly correct in general that we have been shortlisted for projects worth 30 billion crowns," Kvaerner spokeswoman Marit Ytreeide told Reuters.
The report said Kvaerner was at the forefront of a crucial period for its oil and gas-related activities.
"Kvaerner's ability to secure a good share of this pipeline will to a large extent determine its earnings potential for 1997 and 1998," the analysis said.
"Not least, it will provide some important signals as regards Kvaerner's competitive strengths in this area."
One of the largest contracts up for grabs is for the semi-submersible production vessel for the Aasgard oil development in the Norwegian Sea.
Kvaerner is shortlisted for the project along with Norway's Aker Maritime ASA and Brown & Root, the report said.
"It's a big challenge to seize these opportunities," Kvaerner's Ytreeide said.
